protocol: 2400 AdamW steps at 3e-3, batch 64, ~120k parameters, 3 seeds, train lengths 8-16, evaluated at 64

C1_composition_works.measured: 0.692, the best of any architecture tested, up from 0.652

C2_no_column_is_sacrificed.required: within 0.15 of the per-task best on every task
C2_no_column_is_sacrificed.measured: parity gap 0.000, mod_sum 0.002, copy 0.130, needle 0.023 -- but REVERSE gap 0.225 (0.146 against 0.371)

the_finding_the_failure_produced: CAPABILITY COMPETITION IS CONSERVED. Adding the third route did exactly what C3 predicted -- it
relieved the state-tracking / retrieval conflict, taking mod_sum from 0.776 to 0.998 while needle
stayed at 0.977. And it simultaneously destroyed the third capability: reverse fell to 0.146,
which is chance, from 0.348 for the cursor alone and 0.371 for the LSTM alone.
The conflict was not resolved. It moved.

the_frontier_gap.correction_note: An earlier draft of this record said 72%, from an arithmetic error on my part. The correct figure is 90%: the best single architecture reaches 0.692 of a collective frontier of 0.768. The AGGREGATE gap is therefore modest, and the competition claim rests on the PER-TASK pattern rather than on the mean.
the_frontier_gap.per_task_evidence: cursor_attn scores 0.146 on reverse where cursor alone scores 0.348 and the LSTM alone scores 0.371; it scores 0.998 on mod_sum where the two-route hybrid scores 0.776. Adding a route moved which column was sacrificed.

consequence: The kill condition applies: capability competition is a property of the training objective rather
than of any particular pairing of routes, and no mechanism tested resolves it. Nova terminates on
Two of the three leading architectures are prior-art compositions (attention-augmented RNN; NTM
location addressing). The third, cursor_attn, is a composition of both.
